text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Greek Cypriot press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- There has been no progress during proximity talks on the substance of the Cyprus issue, the government spokesman says.
- Attorney-general urges parliament to speed up its examination of government draft legislation decriminalising homosexuality.
- Democratic Party leader Spyros Kyprianou questions why it took the axed justice minister so long to accuse him of interference in police promotions and appointments.
- Hoteliers call for a more competitive tourism product.
- SEK trade union sets sails for the re-election of (President Glafcos) Clerides, describing his proposal on the modification of cost of living allowance as a "victory for the trade union movement".
- Cyprus shivers under unprecedented cold weather for April.
- Opposition parties are due to meet today to clarify their intentions on their cooperation during the forthcoming presidential elections.
- Bounced cheques reached 200 million pounds last year, up 50 percent on 1995.
- United Nations Secretary-General Kofi Annan wants talks between Clerides and (Turkish Cypriot leader Rauf) Denktash in June, while the government says the impasse has not been breached.
